block.title: The C lexer and parser run in Gallina through both OCaml and λANF
block.p: The C lexer, attribute classification table, C parser, and canonical Prolog serializer now exist in pure, zero-axiom Gallina in CLex.v, CAttrs.v, CParse.v, and CCanon.v. They port c_lex.pl, c_parse.pl, and the attribute table of c_types.pl without pattern matching on string or character literals, so both standard OCaml extraction and CertiRocq's λANF lowering map comparisons onto native equality primitives.

CertiRocq taps the full frontend driver into 5.2 MB of λANF in 17 seconds. AnfLower.v lowers those 2,412 hoisted functions into 1,376 checked nanofil IR functions (9.1 MB) in 4 seconds using only the existing arena primitives, and nanofil-backend compile-allocated validates and emits 989,080 lines of Fil-C x86-64 assembly in 3 seconds. On swa (Ryzen 9 7950X3D), both the OCaml extraction and the Fil-C arena binary match SWI-Prolog byte-for-byte across all 487 C test files, 9 C23 files, and 48 Fil-C glibc preprocessed translation units (4.60 MB, 644,822 tokens, 22,173 AST items). Running the arena binary with a 4096-word nursery under FUGC_SCRIBBLE=1 FUGC_VERIFY=1 completed 11,767 minor collections across the 487-file corpus without traps.

claim.p: The extracted OCaml C frontend matches SWI-Prolog byte-for-byte on all 487 C test fixtures and 9 C23 fixtures.
The λANF-lowered Fil-C frontend binary matches OCaml and SWI-Prolog byte-for-byte across all 487 C test fixtures and 48 Fil-C glibc preprocessed translation units.

metrics.baseline: SWI-Prolog on 48 Fil-C glibc .i units (4.60 MB, 644k tokens, swa)
